title: Quantum Sampling of Random Spanning Trees via Amortized Data Structures
authors: Yassine Hamoudi, Adrian Tanasa, Shrinidhi Teganahally Sridhara
abstract: We present a quantum algorithm that generates a uniform superposition over the spanning trees of a graph -- also known as a q-sample -- using only a sub-linear number of queries to the graph. This goes beyond previous work that focuses on generating classical samples, including a recent quantum algorithm by Apers, Gao, Ji, and Liu [ICALP 2025]. For an $n$-vertex, $m$-edge graph, our algorithm admits a pre-processing step of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{mn} + m^{1-δ})$, after which each q-sample can be generated in $\tilde{O}(n^{1+2δ})$ for any $δ$. Alternatively, $k$ independent q-samples can be generated at a total cost of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{kmn})$. We also prove a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors, showing that our algorithm is essentially optimal. Further tradeoffs are given in the paper. In comparison, the optimal classical algorithms (Anari, Liu and Vuong [FOCS 2022]) need an $\tilde{O}(m)$ pre-processing step, after which each sample costs $\tilde{O}(n)$ operations. These results yield faster quantum walk-based algorithms for counting spanning trees or finding a marked one.   Our result is obtained via quantum walk sampling over a sequence of slowly-changing Markov chains. Each chain is an isotropized up-down walk that mixes rapidly to the spanning tree distribution of the input graph. A key ingredient is an amortized data structure supporting fast implementation of the associated quantum walk operators throughout the sequence. This data structure maintains access to a spectral sparsifier and a leverage score sampler that evolve with the underlying graph.
summary: This paper presents a quantum algorithm to efficiently sample a uniform superposition over the spanning trees of a graph. It achieves a sub-linear query complexity by employing quantum walks over a sequence of slowly changing Markov chains. This work provides a quantum advantage over classical methods for graph sampling and has implications for quantum counting algorithms.
main_problem: Developing an efficient quantum algorithm to generate a uniform superposition over all spanning trees of a given graph.
main_result: The authors achieve a quantum sampling complexity of $	ilde{O}(\sqrt{mn})$ queries for the q-sample, which is shown to be essentially optimal via a matching lower bound.
method: The algorithm employs quantum walk sampling over a sequence of slowly-changing Markov chains, utilizing an amortized data structure to maintain spectral sparsifiers and leverage score samplers.
model_or_system: The system is a weighted connected graph $G=(V, E, w)$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The target state is a uniform superposition over the spanning trees, $|\piangle$.
key_observables: Query complexity, spectral gap ($\gamma_{	ext{ph}}$), and the resulting q-sample state $|\piangle$.
important_parameters: Graph size ($n, m$), number of samples ($k$), and the required query complexity bounds ($	ilde{O}(\sqrt{mn})$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of an admissible spanning tree $S$ and the ability to compute necessary spectral sparsifiers.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general quantum walk theory and spectral analysis (showing phase gap bounds) to the specific application of quantum sampling via a cooling schedule and amortized data structures.
why_interesting: The use of quantum walks and spectral sparsifiers to solve a complex combinatorial sampling problem demonstrates advanced techniques in quantum algorithms applicable to many physical systems modeled by graphs.
